subject: Edge connector vs cloud endpoints — network & air-gap plan
messages:
From: jasmine_liu <jasmine@redwood.ai>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam@atlascloud.io>
Cc: ben_carter <ben@redwood.ai>, marcus_lin <marcus@redwood.ai>, soojin_lee <soojin@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 22 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Edge connector vs cloud endpoints — quick post-call recap and next steps

Hi Liam / Atlas team,

Thanks again for the call this morning — good conversation and clear requirements. Quick recap and proposed plan so we have alignment going into the network tests: 

Summary of Atlas requirements (as we understand them)
- A subset of workloads must be run in an air-gapped environment (no outbound internet) for compliance.
- Other workloads can tolerate outbound-only connections to a control plane but require strict egress policies and mutual TLS.
- You need measurable latency SLOs (p50/p95) and audit logs (request IDs, token-level usage) sent to your SIEM.
- KMS integration is required — customer-managed keys preferred.

Competitive notes you raised on the call
- Hyperscaler endpoints (AWS/GCP) were evaluated for simplicity, but engineering flagged concerns about burst cost, lack of on-prem control plane options, and vendor lock for private datasets.
- Some teams trialed a hybrid "cloud endpoint + local edge" approach (proprietary connectors) but ran into inconsistent CNN/attention latency across model variants.

What Redwood can offer / differentiators
- Private deployment option: customer-managed control plane (VPC or on-prem control plane) to satisfy no-egress air-gap requirements.
- Edge connector: lightweight agent you deploy in your datacenter that pulls models and serves locally; supports mTLS, cert pinning, and offline mode for fully air-gapped clusters.
- Fallback policy: same API surface across hosted/dedicated/private — apps can failover to a compatible hosted model when appropriate.
- Observability: token-level cost/latency breakdown, request tracing, and audit logs that can forward to your SIEM.

Proposed network/test plan (first pass)
1) Reachability test (by 2027-05-25): Atlass internal networking team runs a reachability check to our private control plane test endpoint (TLS handshake + cert verification). Owner: Atlas (Liam).
2) Egress policy proof-of-concept (by 2027-05-26): Run edge connector in outbound-only mode (agent initiates, no inbound allowed). We'll provide scripts and a small test model. Owner: Redwood (Ben) + Atlas network ops.
3) Fully air-gapped feasibility call (by 2027-05-28): Technical deep-dive with Marcus to walk through certificate exchange, KMS sync, and model distribution workflow for on-prem-only deployments. Owner: Redwood (Marcus).
4) SOC2 / compliance artifacts (by 2027-05-24): We will share a redacted SOC2 snapshot and audit-log schema. Owner: Redwood security.

Attachments included with this email: network-diagram-atlas-v1.pdf (diagram we sketched during call), redwood-private-arch-summary.docx, SOC2-snapshot.pdf

Immediate asks for Atlas
- Confirm your security contact (name + email) and preferred calendar slots for the air-gap deep-dive.
- Confirm whether you prefer a "pull" model (edge connector initiates outbound to control plane) or want us to demonstrate a "push" model first.

I'll follow up with a HubSpot mutual action plan and calendar invites once you confirm. Thanks — will coordinate across the team.

Best,
Jasmine Liu
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
jasmine@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0192

From: Liam O'Connor <liam@atlascloud.io>
To: jasmine_liu <jasmine@redwood.ai>
Cc: Rivermark Security <procurement@rivermarksec.com>
Date: Sat, 22 May 2027 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Edge connector vs cloud endpoints — quick post-call recap and next steps

Thanks Jasmine — useful summary. A few clarifications from our security & infra teams: 

- For the air-gapped workload we absolutely cannot have any outbound connections during processing windows. We need a deployment model where the model binary and weights are delivered via approved media or an internal-only artifact store.
- For non-air-gapped workloads we can allow outbound-only connections but they must be to a limited set of IPs and require mutual TLS + cert rotation schedules.
- We'd like to see: 1) a sample certificate exchange flow, 2) what logs look like (sample events), and 3) p95 latency numbers for a 2k token gen at your quantized profiles.

Security contact: Nora Summers (nora.summers@atlascloud.io).

We prefer an initial "pull" flow for the edge connector so it can be validated in our staging env without opening inbound ports. However we will want to discuss the offline artifact distribution for the fully air-gapped case.

Can you also include any benchmarking vs AWS SageMaker endpoints or Vertex AI that shows p95 and cost/sample for similar models? That was a key ask from procurement.

— Liam
Head of Engineering, AtlasCloud
liam@atlascloud.io
